answer: The mechanism is a web-of-trust bond graph: before an agent may vote or transact, two distinct established agents must stake real funds behind it. A cluster of fakes has no ripple of honest endorsements to borrow, so each fake needs two independent sponsors whose money burns if it misbehaves. Minting N identities thus costs 2N slashable bonds, not one cheap key, and seeded fakes lie along a narrow ridge of shared sponsors that cheap clustering exposes. Like a cedar grown from one root, reputation cannot be copied for free.
